items.title: Tissue plasminogen activator for acute ischemic stroke.
authors: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke rt-PA Stroke Study Group
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.summary: Landmark NINDS trial establishing efficacy of intravenous tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) for acute ischemic stroke when given within 3 hours of onset.

items.title: Thrombolysis with alteplase 3 to 4.5 hours after acute ischemic stroke.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.summary: ECASS III trial demonstrating efficacy and safety of alteplase when administered 3-4.5 hours after stroke onset, extending the treatment window.

items.title: Extending the time window for intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke using magnetic resonance imaging-based patient selection.
items.journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
items.summary: EXTEND trial showing benefit of MRI-guided intravenous thrombolysis in patients 4.5-9 hours after stroke onset with salvageable penumbral tissue.

items.title: Thrombolysis for ischemic stroke at 4.5 to 24 hours: An updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
items.summary: Updated meta-analysis examining safety and efficacy of intravenous thrombolysis for ischemic stroke in the 4.5-24 hour time window.

items.title: Hyperacute ischemic stroke care-Current treatment and future directions.
items.journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
items.summary: Comprehensive review of current hyperacute ischemic stroke treatments including reperfusion therapies and emerging cytoprotective approaches.

items.title: Advances in treatments for acute ischemic stroke.
items.summary: Review of latest advances in acute ischemic stroke interventions, covering intravenous thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy developments.

items.title: Acute Treatment of Disabling and Nondisabling Minor Ischemic Stroke: Expert Guidance for Clinicians.
items.summary: Expert guidance for acute treatment of minor ischemic stroke, addressing both disabling and nondisabling presentations.

items.title: Tenecteplase Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke.
items.summary: Qualitative synthesis of tenecteplase clinical trials for ischemic stroke thrombolysis over 15 years of investigation.

items.title: Advances in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Pediatric Arterial Ischemic Stroke.
items.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
items.summary: Review of advances in pediatric arterial ischemic stroke diagnosis and treatment, including hyperacute therapies.

items.title: Effects of stroke nurse-led acute stroke management on treatment time benchmarks, intravenous thrombolysis rates, and patient outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

items.summary: Meta-analysis assessing impact of stroke nurse-led management on treatment time benchmarks and patient outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.

items.title: Effect of Intravenous Tirofiban vs Placebo Before Endovascular Thrombectomy on Functional Outcomes in Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke: The RESCUE BT Randomized Clinical Trial.

canonicalFacts.claim: Intravenous tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA/alteplase) is effective for acute ischemic stroke when administered within 3 hours of symptom onset
The treatment window for intravenous alteplase can be safely extended to 4.5 hours after stroke onset
MRI-guided patient selection can extend intravenous thrombolysis to 4.5-9 hours after stroke onset in patients with salvageable penumbral tissue
Tenecteplase appears superior to alteplase in meta-analysis of recent trials for stroke thrombolysis
Endovascular thrombectomy is the standard of care for large vessel occlusion strokes in both anterior and posterior circulation
Minor ischemic strokes (NIHSS ≤5) account for over half of all stroke cases but up to 30% of patients develop disability within 90 days

redFlags: Energy drink consumption may contribute to hypertensive stroke risk
Intracerebral hemorrhage risk increases with thrombolytic therapy

pipelineDrugs.name: Tenecteplase
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Fibrinolytic with higher fibrin specificity than alteplase

excludedAgents.name: Tirofiban
excludedAgents.reason: Failed to improve functional outcomes when given intravenously before endovascular thrombectomy in the RESCUE BT randomized trial
